slides.text: A slice can hold other slices, and that is how Go makes a grid. Each row is a slice of its own, so rows can have different lengths and a row can be shared. You will build grids, walk them and see what a row shares.

A grid in Go is a slice whose values are slices. Each row is its own slice, so rows can have different lengths, unlike a grid of arrays.

The snippet is pseudo code, not Go.
slides.code:
grid = list of rows
    row 0 = 1, 2, 3
    row 1 = 4, 5
grid at row 1, place 0 = 4

slides.text: Because a row is a slice, a `make` for the grid only makes the outer list. Every row still has to be made.
